annotations.title: Check if a property is overpaying

description: BusinessRateChecker's verdict on whether a property's rateable value looks high against comparable properties, exactly as on the website report: strong_case, worth_checking, no_obvious_issues, not_enough_evidence or needs_turnover (with the website's wording in label, and flagged as on the overpayment map), with a suggested rateable value and indicative annual saving where there is one (and, where transitional relief probably caps this year's bill, the saving after it), the confidence, the hedge text that must be relayed with any figure, and a scheme_check showing how the VO's own valuation scheme values similar-sized properties (a saving on a property that sits within its scheme's range is a weak case on rate alone). Pass sole_property=false for a ratepayer with other business properties (Small Business Rate Relief then does not apply) or true if this is their only one. Also carries everything the full report sets out: grounds (every finding with its evidence), checks (rateable value, floor area, allowances, reliefs), route (Check, Challenge, Tribunal), next_steps, track_record (how Checks, Challenges and tribunal appeals on this kind of property have gone, England and Wales) and council_cases (how Checks and Challenges go in the property's council: the VOA's settled cases and the share that cut the value, with the median yearly saving on the 2026 list). Same engine as the website report. Costs 5 credits (one verdict per property per day).

include.description: Optional extra sections for the answer. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.include_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored. Leave out unless the user asks for something the normal answer lacks.

options.description: Optional extra settings by name. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.options_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored.

property_id.description: The property_id from find_properties (the Valuation Office assessment reference), or a UARN, 4 to 15 digits. A UARN that covers several entries returns them all.

sole_property.description: true if this is the ratepayer's only business property, false if they occupy others. Omit if unknown, then ask before quoting the Small Business Rate Relief figure.
